findings.text: blocking: the moved resolver block defines _is_executable_file a second time (the pre-existing definition is at :681) and _SHELL_ASSIGNMENT a second time (pre-existing at :417), so the change whose purpose is one owner of the executable test leaves two in the same module, and the later definition silently shadows the earlier.

non-blocking: the guard resolves with roots only while the replay at :1272 passes tree and interpreter, so the docstring's claim that the two cannot drift does not hold: a .venv/bin/python command the replay would resolve through the measuring interpreter is refused at promotion.

non-blocking: the guard still tokenises the command itself and reports argv[0] as the program, so an env-wrapped command that fails to resolve is refused naming env rather than the interpreter the shared resolver reported.

non-blocking: rewrite_gate_program substitutes the first regex occurrence anywhere in the command, so a quoted argument naming the interpreter before the program token is rewritten instead of the program, contradicting the docstring at :598 that says an occurrence inside an argument is left alone.

non-blocking: the control the manifest names as negative_control_log carries no revision header, no literal command line and no closing EXIT= line, so the tree it ran against cannot be read from the log.

non-blocking: the sentence reads "this is not a shell from the merge", which says the opposite of the node's point; it should state that the message makes clear the failure did not come from the merge.
